name: Digit
summary: Inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system for manufacturers and distributors, rebranded from Digit to Sutton in September 2026 (same company, same terms; digit-software.com now redirects to heysutton.com).
best_for: manufacturers and distributors outgrowing spreadsheets who need inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system, and who genuinely need lot tracking and traceability rather than just wanting them
skip_if: you are a small operation where $400/month for five users is heavy against what a warehouse module in your existing accounting package would cost; also skip it if your integration list is long, because the per-connection model punishes exactly that — $100 to $125 a month for every integration past the second, depending on which part of their pricing page you read
honest_knock: The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling, and the add-ons are where an inventory system quietly doubles. Two integrations are included — but a working setup usually means an accounting package and a webshop, which is your two, and then Amazon or a second sales channel is another $125 a month by the FAQ (the integrations block on the same page still says $100; we have asked which one bills). Want the API, or your data inside an AI assistant? $125 a month each. A Starter customer on QuickBooks, Shopify and Amazon with API access is at $650 a month on the FAQ's numbers, $625 on the block's, before adding a sixth user. Price the whole configuration you actually need, not the tier.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-09-17 in a rendered browser on heysutton.com/pricing, the rebranded site; unchanged from the 5 September reading on digit-software.com) Four tiers with three published: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15, and Enterprise on quote. Extra users are $63/month each on every tier. Paying quarterly takes 10% off — $360, $675 and $1,170 a month, shown with the quarter total beside it — and annually 20%, which is $320, $600 and $1,040 with the year total beside it; the page now opens on Monthly, so the first figure you see is the real monthly rate. Two integrations are included on every plan. The third and each one after it is where the page disagrees with itself: the Integrations block says $100 a month, the FAQ on the same page says $125, and the add-on cards side with the FAQ — API access $125 a month, MCP access $125, push notifications and webhooks $63, all the same price on Starter, Growth and Professional. Customer portals are $18.75 per portal per month on every tier, Enterprise included. We asked Digit which of the two they bill on 5 September 2026 and had no answer; twelve days later, on the rebranded site, both figures were still there.

compare_with.name: Katana
compare_with.why: the natural head-to-head for manufacturers leaving spreadsheets. Both cover inventory and production; the difference shows up in how they charge for the edges. Price the full configuration you need on each — every integration, the API if you want it — because Digit's per-connection add-ons — $100 to $125 a month for each integration past the first two, and $125 for API or MCP access — are where the tier price stops being the price
